_preregistration.primary: does either model move robustly UP under one domain and robustly DOWN under another, from a single raw value, each shift judged against its OWN seed noise
_preregistration.why: F149 could not test the floor/ceiling account because 5 of 6 models sat at an extreme; F150 screened for models with genuine headroom and found these two
_preregistration.note: a new file on purpose -- domain_gradient.py's model list is NOT edited, because its provenance closure is stamped into F147's and F148's stored results and widening it in place would invalidate them; the census, wrapper and prose sampler are imported unchanged so the quantity is identical

verdict: RUNG (raw arm reproduces midrange_screen): 4 cells compared, worst error 0.00e+00. Identical, so this is F150's measurement with only the domain varying. ANTI-VACUITY (checked, not assumed): 0 of 2 models lack room to move both ways beyond tolerance, so both models can in principle show either direction. PRIMARY, bidirectionality from a single raw value (weights and starting point FIXED, only the domain varying, each shift against its own seed noise): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct raw 0.573 [funnel] -> bos -0.562 (down, tol 0.042, none), text_matched -0.562 (down, tol 0.042, none), chat_template -0.557 (down, tol 0.062, none), prose:corpus0 -0.562 (down, tol 0.042, none), prose:corpus1 -0.339 (down, tol 0.146, borderline), prose:corpus2 -0.547 (down, tol 0.042, none), prose:shak0 -0.542 (down, tol 0.083, none), prose:shak1 -0.562 (down, tol 0.042, none), prose:shak2 -0.484 (down, tol 0.146, UNSTABLE); gemma-2-2b-it raw 0.714 [fragmented] -> bos -0.677 (down, tol 0.042, none), text_matched -0.266 (down, tol 0.125, borderline), chat_template -0.714 (down, tol 0.042, none), prose:corpus0 -0.266 (down, tol 0.125, borderline), prose:corpus1 -0.286 (down, tol 0.125, funnel), prose:corpus2 -0.630 (down, tol 0.125, UNSTABLE), prose:shak0 -0.708 (down, tol 0.042, none), prose:shak1 -0.552 (down, tol 0.042, borderline), prose:shak2 -0.417 (down, tol 0.042, UNSTABLE). NEITHER model moves both ways, and unlike F149 these models COULD have. That is a much stronger null: on models with genuine headroom the domain still moves everything one way, so the deflationary account survives a test designed to break it. SECONDARY, the kind contrast at matched length on two FRESH models (F147's test, prose read as an ensemble per F148): Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct template 0.016 vs prose [0.010, 0.234], closest prose 0.005 away; gemma-2-2b-it template 0.000 vs prose [0.005, 0.448], closest prose 0.005 away. A prose range that does not reach the template value extends F147's contrast to models it was not fitted on; one that straddles it bounds the contrast instead. FIRST FRAGMENTED MODEL in any domain run (['gemma-2-2b-it']): classes across its domains are gemma-2-2b-it bos=none, text_matched=borderline, chat_template=none, prose:corpus0=borderline, prose:corpus1=funnel, prose:corpus2=UNSTABLE, prose:shak0=none, prose:shak1=borderline, prose:shak2=UNSTABLE. F144's class claim had only ever been tested on funnels and nones, so this is new coverage of the taxonomy regardless of what the PRIMARY returns. BOUNDARY: 2 models, 96 starts, 2 census seeds, one prose ensemble per F148. The PRIMARY is an existence test either way: it can refute a general floor/ceiling account or fail to, but two models cannot say how common either is.
